name: quickjs
title: QuickJS 2025-04-26 (Fabrice Bellard), a JavaScript engine compiled to JavaScript
fetch: mkdir -p corpus/quickjs && curl -Lo corpus/quickjs/quickjs-2025-04-26.tar.xz https://bellard.org/quickjs/quickjs-2025-04-26.tar.xz && tar -xJf corpus/quickjs/quickjs-2025-04-26.tar.xz -C corpus/quickjs && node tools/build.mjs targets/quickjs.json:qjsc --run --data=corpus/quickjs/quickjs-2025-04-26 --out=corpus/quickjs/quickjs-2025-04-26 '--args=-s -c -o repl.c -m repl.js'
_doc: A JavaScript engine, run by the JavaScript engine it is compiled into. Here as an ORACLE as much as a target, as Lua is: QuickJS ships its own self-checking tests (tests/*.js, built on assert), and its compiler qjsc turns JavaScript into bytecode as a C array -- a byte-for-byte comparable output, against a native build of the same qjsc.
_units: The Makefile's QJS_LIB_OBJS; each program adds its own main. qjs also links repl.c, which the Makefile GENERATES with qjsc from repl.js (`qjsc -s -c -o repl.c -m repl.js`) -- so qjsc is built first and generates it, as the fetch line does.

qjsc.title: qjsc, the QuickJS compiler (JavaScript to bytecode in C)

_defines: The Makefile's DEFINES on a non-Windows host.
_env: pthread: quickjs-libc's os.Worker and quickjs.c's Atomics.wait are POSIX threads. environ: std.getenviron walks it.
